title: Italian plague of 1629–1631
summary: From 1629, plague spread through northern Italy, brought by imperial troops marching toward the siege of Mantua. Milan recorded its first cases that October and its most devastating epidemic in 1630. Venice had a massive outbreak in late 1630 that lasted into autumn 1631. A study of 56 Italian cities links the epidemic to lasting damage to urban populations and urbanization.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 1629 arrival in Milan (first cases from 9 October 1629). End is the Venetian tail into autumn 1631 (Lazzari et al. 2020); the sources give no single end date for the whole epidemic, and Milan's 1630 register deaths run to 30 December 1630 (Galli et al. 2023).
